decisions.title: Bounded lossless AMQP message mapping
decisions.issue: AMQP field tables and basic properties expose more wire representations than the public language-neutral message model can preserve safely.
interpretations: Preserve one bounded language-neutral subset and reject unsupported representations
decisions.peer_behavior: The pinned php-amqplib v3.7.4 live-broker harness exchanges the same fixture in both directions; unsupported nested field-table values remain outside the shared corpus.
decisions.selected_behavior: Preserve opaque body bytes, bounded string, boolean, byte, uint16, and uint32 field-table values, normalize unsigned integers to non-negative int64, preserve whole-second timestamps, and distinguish omitted expiration from explicit zero while rejecting unsupported or over-limit metadata.
decisions.rationale: A small explicit mapping prevents silent precision, presence, type, and allocation changes across Go and PHP clients.
decisions.security_consequences: Header counts, names, values, body bytes, and broker-owned metadata are bounded before allocation or exposure.
decisions.resource_consequences: The package applies fixed maximums and caller-reducible limits to every mapped field.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Adding a field-table type or changing integer, timestamp, or expiration representation requires a compatibility review.
decisions.wire_consequences: Supported metadata and body bytes round-trip without coercion; sub-second timestamps and unsupported field-table shapes are rejected before publication.
decisions.upstream_status: AMQP 0-9-1 defines the wire types; the narrower public mapping is package policy.
decisions.reconsider_when: A supported peer or application requires another AMQP field-table type without weakening deterministic bounds.

decisions.title: Publisher confirms and mandatory returns form one outcome
decisions.issue: A mandatory unroutable publication can receive both a basic.return and a positive publisher confirmation, and callback order does not by itself define one application outcome.
interpretations: Treat the positive confirmation as acceptance
Treat the first callback as final
Correlate both callbacks to the exact publication before reporting one result
decisions.peer_behavior: The pinned php-amqplib v3.7.4 harness confirms routed publications through RabbitMQ 4.3, while the Go live-broker suite separately proves mandatory-return reconciliation.
decisions.selected_behavior: Enable publisher confirms, attach an exact private correlation token, reconcile mandatory returns before a positive confirmation, and report an unroutable publication as returned rather than confirmed.
decisions.rationale: A broker acknowledgement of processing is not evidence that a mandatory message reached a queue.
decisions.security_consequences: Broker return text and package correlation metadata are not exposed as application-controlled diagnostics.
decisions.resource_consequences: Outstanding correlations are bounded by MaxOutstanding and released on every terminal generation path.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Applications can distinguish confirmed, returned, rejected, not-sent, and ambiguous outcomes without callback-order races.
decisions.wire_consequences: Mandatory publication uses RabbitMQ confirms plus a package-owned header that is stripped from deliveries.
decisions.upstream_status: RabbitMQ documents confirms and mandatory returns as related but distinct protocol effects.
decisions.reconsider_when: RabbitMQ introduces a single authoritative routed-publication outcome or changes confirm and return ordering guarantees.

decisions.title: Post-transmission failure remains ambiguous
decisions.section: Publisher Confirms and When Will Published Messages Be Confirmed
decisions.issue: Connection loss or context cancellation after client transmission can hide whether RabbitMQ accepted the publication.
interpretations: Report every local error as not sent
Assume every transmitted message was accepted
Preserve an explicit ambiguous outcome until application reconciliation
decisions.peer_behavior: RabbitMQ clients generally cannot recover a missing publisher confirmation after their channel or connection is lost.
decisions.selected_behavior: Report not-sent only before client transmission; after transmission, cancellation, channel loss, and missing terminal confirmation produce PublishAmbiguous unless a definitive return or confirmation was already observed.
decisions.rationale: Retrying an uncertain publication as definitely absent can duplicate an accepted message.
decisions.security_consequences: Sanitized ambiguity reporting does not expose broker, endpoint, credential, or payload details.
decisions.resource_consequences: Generation failure completes every outstanding attempt once and bounds retained state.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Callers must reconcile or idempotently retry ambiguous outcomes instead of treating them as definite failures.
decisions.wire_consequences: The package does not emit a compensating AMQP frame or automatic duplicate publication after an uncertain send.
decisions.upstream_status: No protocol method reconstructs an unobserved confirmation after channel loss.
decisions.reconsider_when: A supported RabbitMQ protocol extension provides durable publication identity and authoritative outcome recovery.

decisions.title: Manual settlement preserves bounded at-least-once delivery
decisions.section: Basic.Ack, Basic.Reject, Basic.Recover, and consumer acknowledgements
decisions.issue: AMQP permits automatic or manual acknowledgement and repeated requeue, but neither choice defines a bounded application failure policy.
interpretations: Settle after the handler with an explicit bounded failure policy
decisions.peer_behavior: Maintained AMQP clients expose manual acknowledgement primitives but leave handler timing and retry limits to applications.
decisions.selected_behavior: Use per-consumer manual acknowledgement, settle only after handler completion, preserve explicit ack, nack, reject, and delegate choices, and cap requeue using RabbitMQ delivery counters before applying the configured terminal failure policy.
decisions.rationale: Post-handler settlement provides at-least-once processing without an unbounded poison-message loop.
decisions.security_consequences: Malformed broker counters and settlement metadata fail closed without exposing broker text.
decisions.resource_consequences: Prefetch, concurrency, handler duration, requeue attempts, and settlement waits are bounded.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Handlers must be idempotent and must not assume that connection loss prevents concurrent redelivery.
decisions.wire_consequences: The consumer emits one Basic.Ack, Basic.Nack, or Basic.Reject for a tracked generation delivery, or leaves it to channel closure only when explicitly delegated.
decisions.upstream_status: AMQP defines settlement methods; retry budgets and handler ownership remain application policy.
decisions.reconsider_when: RabbitMQ changes delivery counter semantics or a supported settlement mode can prove a stronger bounded guarantee.

decisions.title: Queue capabilities and topology mutation are explicit
decisions.section: Queue Types, Declaration and Property Equivalence, and Temporary Queues
decisions.issue: RabbitMQ classic and quorum queues support different declaration arguments, defaults, and lifecycle constraints, while active declaration can mutate broker topology.
interpretations: Pass every option to every queue type
Rely on RabbitMQ defaults and active declaration
Validate queue-specific capabilities and require explicit authority before topology mutation
decisions.peer_behavior: RabbitMQ 4.3 rejects or ignores incompatible queue arguments depending on the feature; ordinary AMQP clients expose declarations without package-level environment policy.
decisions.selected_behavior: Require an explicit classic or quorum queue type, validate only type-supported arguments, preserve omitted versus explicit quorum delivery limits, use passive topology by default, and permit declarations and bindings only under an explicit development topology capability.
decisions.rationale: Preflight capability checks and explicit mutation authority prevent silent broker defaults, ignored policy, and production topology drift.
decisions.security_consequences: Application configuration cannot silently gain topology mutation authority or create unsupported queue policies.
decisions.resource_consequences: Queue names, TTLs, lengths, delivery limits, timeouts, retry delays, and topology collections are bounded before broker calls.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: New RabbitMQ queue types or arguments require an explicit capability and migration decision rather than generic pass-through.
decisions.wire_consequences: Passive checks preserve broker state; authorized development mode emits declarations with deterministic type-specific argument presence.
decisions.upstream_status: RabbitMQ 4.3 documents queue-type property equivalence and feature differences; mutation authority remains package policy.
decisions.reconsider_when: RabbitMQ changes classic or quorum declaration equivalence, adds a supported queue type, or standardizes a safe topology ownership protocol.
